title: Germany news: Doctors offer Oktoberfest flu jabs
summary: Oktoberfest 2026 is underway but it's not just beer on offer in Munich this year; revelers can also get themselves a flu jab before heading to the tents. DW has more.
byline: Matt Ford, Rana Taha, Timothy Jones

image.caption: Munich mayor Dominik Krause had the honor of tapping the first beer keg to officially open OktoberfestImage: Sven Hoppe/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: O'piekst is!: German doctors offer Oktoberfest flu jabs

blocks.caption: Tightly packed groups of revelers raise trhe risk of the spread of illnessImage: Felix Hörhager/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Munich's annual Oktoberfest officially got underway on Saturday when the first beer keg was opened with the traditional cry of O'zapft is! ("It has been tapped!").
But another slogan is also being promoted in Bavaria this year: O'piekst is! ("It has been pricked!") — as doctors offer vaccine jabs against flu and Covid-19.

"With so many people coming together in such tight spaces in the beer tents, the risk of infection at Oktoberfest is higher," explained Christoph Spinner, head of infectiology at Munich's Rechts der Isar hospital.
Oktoberfest coincides with the start of the annual flu season, and Spinner warned that less than a third of people who are recommended a flu jab have actually had one.
Beatrix Zurek, a health expert from the city-led initiative München impft! ("Munich vaccinates!") said: "It's our job to go where people are. And that means: Oktoberfest."
